messages:
Oliver Chen: Quick async check for YYZ onboarding — egress / routing / residency items. TL;DR: peering and NAT are up, but we still need a tiny egress ACL update for telemetry endpoints + confirm KMS routing for residency-sensitive customers. Calling out owners: @Jia, @Rachel. Can you two own the follow-ups?

Jia Patel: Ack. Status: VPC peering is done, NAT GW provisioned. I think the telemetry vendor uses a handful of IP ranges (CDN & ingest). Samir, did you add those ranges to infra?

Samir Khan: Yep — I pushed a PR to infra/terraform: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2876 (small ACL list). Snippet below for quick review:

```
resource "redwood_egress_rule" "datadog" {
  name        = "datadog-ingest"
  cidr_blocks = ["13.32.0.0/16", "34.200.0.0/14"]
  ports       = [443]
  description = "Telemetry -> Datadog / CDN endpoints"
}
```

Samir Khan: That PR also wires the YYZ NAT to the egress ACL. Needs a quick look from infra + security.

Rachel Gomez: KMS / residency note: a few customers require AI workloads to keep keys outside the US. For YYZ we have two options: generate Canada-region keys (recommended) or route encryption ops to EU3 per customer contract. I propose we add a routing tag on our ingress path: `x-residency-preference: canada|eu|us` and then a deterministic KMS routing table.

Nate Li: For model routing fallback — if YYZ capacity is constrained we should prefer USW3 as the secondary region (lower latency vs EU3 for Toronto). That impacts residency only if the customer requires strict in-region compute. For those customers we must enforce no-fallback policy.

Oliver Chen: Agreed on USW3 preference. Action items I' m capturing: 
- Jia: confirm exact telemetry CIDR / do we need to NAT-proxy or just ACLs (due: +8h)
- Samir: request review on infra PR and add a test that validates egress ranges (due: EOD)
- Rachel: draft KMS routing table & residency tag proposal (due: tomorrow noon)
- Nate: document fallback policy and flag enforcement for strict-residency customers (due: next Tue)

Oliver Chen: Quick smoke check for anyone testing the YYZ API — run this locally to confirm residency header and response path:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST_KEY" -H "X-Residence-Hint: canada" https://yyz-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq .
# expect: header X-Resolved-Region: yyz ; X-KMS-Region: ca-central-1
```

deploy-bot: canary deploy to infra/yyz-cluster started at 2791234705 — 3 nodes, image redwood/inference:2026-03-17-canary.

Jia Patel: I looked at the CDN IPs — we only need the two blocks Samir added. I'll confirm with security whether we should proxy. :thumbsup:

Samir Khan: TY. I'll add an e2e that hits the curl above from the staging VPN and asserts the X-Resolved-Region header.

Rachel Gomez: Drafted KMS routing table and pushed to docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/residency/yyz-kms-routing.md. High-level: tag -> primary KMS (ca-central-1) -> fallback none for strict customers. PTAL.

Nate Li: Added fallback policy doc in RFC repo and called out the flag `enforce_strict_residency=true` for customers that opt in. Link: https://github.com/redwood-infra/rfcs/pull/102.

Oliver Chen: Perfect. We'll treat this as async checkpoint. If anything blocks the infra PR merge, @Samir please escalate and ping me. Otherwise I'll mark YYZ as "routing-ready" once Rachel's KMS doc is accepted and Jia confirms the telemetry plan. Thanks all. :rocket:
